items.prompt: I ___ from Spain.
items.explain: With I, always am: I am from Spain.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: I have ___ idea.
items.explain: An before a vowel sound: an idea.

items.prompt: She ___ in a hospital.
items.explain: Third person singular adds -s: she works.

items.prompt: Write the plural: one box, two ___
items.explain: Nouns ending in -x add -es: boxes.

items.prompt: ___ you like coffee?
items.explain: Questions with you use do: Do you like coffee?

items.prompt: Write the missing word: This is Maria. ___ bag is red.
items.explain: Her for something that belongs to a woman.

items.prompt: Listen: what does she have?
items.explain: She said: my sister has two cats.

items.prompt: Listen: when does the bus leave?
items.explain: She said: the bus leaves at seven.

items.speech: Sorry, I can't come today. I am sick.
items.prompt: Listen: what is the problem?
items.explain: She said: I am sick.

items.prompt: Write only the missing word: She ___ my sister. (be)
items.explain: With she, use is.

items.prompt: Write only the plural: one child, two ___
items.explain: Child has an irregular plural: children.

items.prompt: Write the full sentence: I / want / coffee
items.explain: Statement order: I want coffee.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: Yesterday I ___ to the market. (go)
items.explain: Go is irregular in the past: went.

items.prompt: This book is ___ than the film.
items.explain: Good has an irregular comparative: better.

items.prompt: They ___ play football tomorrow.
items.explain: Plans with be + going to + verb: are going to play.

items.prompt: Write much or many: How ___ people came?
items.explain: People is countable, so many.

items.prompt: Write on, in or at: The party is ___ Saturday.
items.explain: Days take on: on Saturday.

items.prompt: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.
items.explain: An action in progress interrupted by a short one: was cooking.

items.speech: We moved here because the rents were cheaper.
items.prompt: Listen: why did they move?
items.explain: She said: because the rents were cheaper.

items.speech: I'll meet you outside the cinema at eight.
items.prompt: Listen: where will they meet?
items.explain: She said: outside the cinema.

items.speech: She's taller than her brother, but he's faster.
items.prompt: Listen: who is faster?
items.explain: She said: he's faster.

items.prompt: Write only the missing word: Last week she ___ a dress. (buy)
items.explain: Buy is irregular: bought.

items.prompt: Write only the comparative of happy:
items.explain: Happy → happier (y → ier).

items.prompt: Write the full sentence: they / play football / tomorrow
answers: They are going to play football tomorrow
They're going to play football tomorrow
They are going to play football
items.explain: Be + going to for plans: They are going to play football tomorrow.

items.prompt: I ___ her since 2019.
items.explain: States that continue up to now take the present perfect: have known.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: If it rains, we ___ stay home. (will/can — one word)
items.explain: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

items.prompt: I ___ live in Rome, but I moved away.
items.explain: Past habits that stopped: used to live.

items.prompt: Write who or which: The film ___ won the prize was French.
items.explain: Which (or that) for things.

items.prompt: The lights are on. They ___ be home.
items.explain: A logical deduction: must be.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: If I ___ more time, I would travel. (have)
items.explain: Second conditional: if + past, would + verb.

items.speech: If it rains tomorrow, we'll postpone the picnic.
items.prompt: Listen: what will they do if it rains?
items.explain: She said: we'll postpone the picnic.

items.speech: He must have forgotten about the meeting; he never showed up.
items.prompt: Listen: what happened?
items.explain: He must have forgotten = a deduction about the past.

items.speech: I would've called you, but my phone died.
items.prompt: Listen: why didn't she call?
items.explain: Would've is the contraction of would have; the reason is the phone died.

items.prompt: Write only the missing word: If I ___ more time, I would travel. (have)
items.explain: Second conditional if-clause takes the past: had.

items.prompt: Write the full sentence: she / never / visit / Rome
items.explain: Present perfect: has + never + past participle.

items.prompt: Write only the missing word: The man ___ called you is my uncle.
items.explain: Who (or that) for people.

items.prompt: The bridge ___ in 1932.
items.explain: Passive past simple: was + built.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: He said he ___ tired. (original: "I am tired")
items.explain: Reported speech shifts am → was.

items.prompt: If I ___ known, I would have called you.
items.explain: Third conditional: if + had + participle.

items.prompt: Write the missing word: I wish I ___ the answer. (know — past form)
items.explain: Wish about the present takes the past: I wish I knew.

items.prompt: They had to ___ the meeting because of the storm.
items.explain: Call off = cancel.

items.prompt: Write one word: ___ the rain, we went out. (= despite)
items.explain: Despite + noun; in spite of means the same.

items.speech: Had I known about the delay, I would have called you.
items.prompt: Listen: did she know about the delay?
items.explain: Had I known... is an inverted third conditional: she did NOT know.

items.speech: She's said to be the best lawyer in town.
items.prompt: Listen: what does the sentence tell us?
items.explain: X is said to be... = reporting what people say, not her own words.

items.speech: The bridge was being repaired, so traffic was diverted.
items.prompt: Listen: why was traffic diverted?
items.explain: Was being repaired = past continuous passive: the repair caused the diversion.

items.prompt: Write the full passive sentence: they / build / the bridge / in 1932
items.explain: Passive past: was + built.

items.prompt: Write only the missing word: I wish I ___ the answer. (know)
items.explain: Wish + past for a present regret: knew.

items.prompt: Write the reported sentence: He said, "I am tired." → He said ___
answers: He said that he was tired
items.explain: Reported: am → was.

items.prompt: Rarely ___ such a clear explanation.
items.explain: A negative adverbial in front position triggers inversion: have we heard.

items.prompt: ___ worries me is the deadline, not the workload.
items.explain: A cleft sentence with What ... is ... focuses the concern.

items.prompt: Write one formal word meaning despite: The risk was real; ___, they proceeded.
items.explain: Nevertheless/nonetheless/however all mark contrast; the sentence needs one after the semicolon.

items.prompt: She ___ have missed the train — she left an hour early.
items.explain: Can't have + participle = a near-certain negative deduction about the past.

items.prompt: The report ___ light on the causes of the failure.
items.explain: Fixed collocation: shed light on something.

items.prompt: Write one word: By June, she ___ have finished the thesis. (will/may — auxiliary of the future perfect)
items.explain: Future perfect: will/may/might/could + have + participle.

items.speech: Not only did the plan fail, but it also backfired.
items.prompt: Listen: what happened to the plan?
items.explain: Not only ... but also ...; backfired = had the opposite, harmful effect.

items.speech: But for your help, the launch would have collapsed.
items.prompt: Listen: what does she mean?
items.explain: But for = if it hadn't been for: an unreal past; the help made the difference.

items.speech: The committee's decision, however controversial, stands.
items.prompt: Listen: what is the status of the decision?
items.explain: However controversial = a concession: despite the controversy, it stands.

items.prompt: Write the full inverted sentence: I have rarely heard such a clear explanation. Start with: Rarely...
answers: Rarely have I heard such a clear explanation
items.explain: Fronted negative adverbial inverts auxiliary and subject: Rarely have I heard...

items.prompt: Complete with one word: But for the storm, we would ___ arrived on time. (have)
items.explain: Would have arrived: the perfect infinitive keeps have after would.

items.prompt: Write one word: She ___ a decision after weighing every option. (make/take collocation)
items.explain: Both make a decision and take a decision are accepted collocations.
